intro: Single-seaters on road circuits that turn both ways. Fast, light and fragile: every hit costs you, a big one can set the car alight or end your race, and the tyres and fuel won't last the distance.
inspiredBy: Open-wheel racing has been around since the early 1900s. Grand Prix is our own take, with our own cars, circuits and drivers.
goal: Be first across the line after the last lap, still in one piece. Races are 5, 10 or 15 laps.
howToPlay: Join with your phone, or race the computer drivers on your own.
In the lobby, choose the circuit, how many computer drivers, how many laps and how quick they are, then press {bolt} to start.
Your phone becomes a steering pad: slide your thumb left and right to steer. Hold {bolt} for gas and {drop} to brake. Brake before the corners, not in them.
Your car has health, tyres and fuel, shown on your screen and your phone. Hits take health, worn tyres grip less, and a damaged car is slower.

Press {l1} to box this lap, then keep to the left of the main straight (follow the dashed line to the ◀ PIT board) and you'll turn into the pit lane. On the way down the lane, choose what the crew does on your phone: ▲▼ picks tyres, fuel or repairs, ◀▶ changes it. The more they do, the longer you wait.
A full tank lasts 7 laps, so longer races need at least one stop. Your phone says when the pit wall thinks you should come in.

Choose the weather in the lobby: Dry, Showers or Rain. When it rains the road gets wet over half a minute and takes a couple of minutes to dry. Slicks are quickest in the dry and slide everywhere in the wet; wets have grooves that clear the water. Box when it changes and the crew fits the right ones: your phone says Wets or Slicks when it's time.
A hard hit can start a fire. A burning car loses health fast: box straight away or it burns out. A really big hit, especially into a barrier at speed, ends your race.
steering: Slide left and right on your phone to steer (or use the arrow keys)
tips: Brake in a straight line, then turn in. Open-wheelers grip well, but not at any speed.
Stopping one lap too late is better than running dry: an empty car can only coast.
Fresh tyres are worth seconds a lap. Sometimes a second stop wins the race.
In the wet, brake earlier: the tyres lock sooner and the car takes longer to stop.
Wets wear out fast once the road dries. Don't stay out on them too long.
Hold {r1} to see who's behind you.
